For the record, Bright was, in fact, originally just a placeholder for "staff person that Maria could yell at". He stayed in when it became apparent that Bright did, in fact, fit the perfect slot for that role (highly-ranked enough to have some responsibility for Omega-7 and Alpha-9, also highly-ranked enough not to feel threatened by Maria's drunken ranting).

Sorry you weren't a fan; I can see how the raw charactsturbation1 wouldn't be for everyone.

Footnotes
1. portmanteu of "characterization" and "masturbation"; I've developed it as a response to a lot of the Resurrection works to date, including my own, as a necessary consequence of the canon at this point in time, hopefully to be unnecessary later

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Interesting in theory, but it feels like a chore for me to personally get through. I'm always a fan of more Maria, but Bright's presence in this tale feels so distracting that at a few points in the tale (particularly that NBC line, as much as I find it rather cool), I wonder if you could replace Bright with an administrator, or an O5, and not make a difference. And above all… it just didn't interest me.

Maria stared at the closed door for two full minutes, then groped around the desk, feeling for her glass. Without looking, she grabbed it and threw the rest of the drink back in one swallow. She collapsed into her chair, soundless tears streaming down her face.

From this point on, I felt hard-pressed to even care, and from the following point on:

"You know, I hate that when other people do that," the voice on the other end replied.

I just can't see why this is something to need. It feels so goddamn drawn out, and superfluous. If its only purpose is set-up, it feels too forced in, and it shows. As well-written as it is, it's too long and not interesting enough to justify the length for me to personally care.

item.content:encoded: This is a direct buildup to the recruiting of Alpha-9 agents, which should build nicely into actual deployments. I know we have people working on more actiony type stuff now (if you don't understand why I wouldn't feel 100% comfortable doing action-type combat scenes, you may have never read the pacing mess that is the latter half of Wayward Prince), and I wanted to get this out before moving on with Maria stuff.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This has been on my mind too… so I'll give some of my thoughts.

The introductory stuff is, essentially, Act 1. Act 1 ends (but can still be contributed to) once all the initial major players are introduced.

You still have a point, though. Basically what's happened is that when planning this, I did not anticipate the deluge of interest and the amount of excellent material people wished to create for it. As a side effect, there IS rather a lot of Introduction stuff.

That said… we at least have conceptualized a whole lot more stuff, of which what you see here is only a small fraction. We'll see how it works out in practice.

Alpha-9 should be officially debuting this coming week.
